name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3 and the composite PMI was 51.7 in October, above 50, though France is contracting
state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct put euro-area GDP growth at 0.4% in the third quarter. The HCOB composite PMI was finalised at 51.7 in October, a four-month low, down from 53.1 in September, with France back in contraction while Germany, Italy and Spain still grew (Tasnim, citing Reuters, 4 Nov). With growth positive, the index above 50 and no technical recession or ECB action against bond-spread fragmentation found as of 28 Nov, the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Conditions are steady for most euro-area households and employers. Firms and workers in France, and in sectors tied to French demand, are the most exposed to the current slowdown in activity.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% and composite PMI 51.7 (Oct) > 50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
Tasnim News — Euro Zone Economic Growth Slows to Four-Month Low in October

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
